$comment: Registered prose invariants for tools/doc-reconcile.mjs, seeded 2026-09-19 (ported from the
Antitube harness's docs/harness/doc-claims.json; the checker's laws came over unchanged).
Each claim binds a SENTENCE in a governed doc to EVIDENCE in code. The gate re-proves the evidence
and re-finds the sentence on every run, so drift in EITHER direction fails: code moving away from
the claim, or the sentence being edited away from the code. When it fails it cannot tell you which
side is wrong — only that they no longer agree. Deciding which to fix is a human's job.
Evidence must point at CODE. A claim proved by another document is the exact failure this gate
exists to prevent: six artifacts once agreed GIVT was an in-process bucket, and they agreed with
each other, which is why it survived. The checker refuses docs/ and .md evidence paths outright.
Seeded with claims whose falsehood has actually cost this project something. Growing this list is
how the gate's reach grows; every load-bearing sentence in README.md and docs/ worth trusting
belongs here eventually.
THE CORPUS A REPO-WIDE CLAIM IS MEASURED AGAINST. Declared here, not hardcoded in the gate,
and printed on every run — the WS1 lesson: upstream, the corpus was hardcoded to two directory
trees, and that is how a claim reading "8 REPO-WIDE" certified a count that was true of those
trees and false of the repo — two more producers lived in tools/, invisible to the arithmetic.
Stallion's honest corpus is the committed repo — tools/, .githooks/, .github/, docs/ and the
manifest — which in this layout means: every tracked file of the extensions below, minus the
declared ignore categories. Markdown is IN the corpus on purpose: stallion governs prose (the
checklist and the wiring guide are load-bearing), so a repo-wide claim must be able to see the
prose surface, even while a claim's EVIDENCE still must be code.
STATED LIMITATION, declared rather than discovered later: the three .githooks scripts
(pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push) carry no file extension, so the extension filter cannot
admit them — a repo-count over shell code is blind to the hooks until they gain an extension
or the corpus grows a names list.
Every ignore entry is a CATEGORY with a reason, never a named file that happened to disagree.
A one-file exclusion belongs on the evidence item that needs it, where the gate prints it.

ignore.why: task records and findings registers are machine-written state — the fence itself classifies them as not code, and counting recorded events would make every new task trip a claim
per-pass lane records generated from the checklist — prose artifacts of completed audits, regenerated per task, never executed
fixture registers consumed by the tools' self-tests, never executed
generated lockfile — a vendored transcription of package.json would double any dependency count

claims.anchor: Every tool here ships a `--self-test` that drives its refusals, not just its happy path
claims.why: Issue #16: a vacuous self-test shipped through a green battery — the self-test existed, the battery never ran it, and nothing failed. Membership is now DERIVED from the tree (dispatchesSelfTest walks tools/ for the dispatch idioms, not a hand-kept list) and the doctor refuses omissions (missingSelfTests); the grep pins the selftest script the CI actually runs.

claims.anchor: The tools are dependency-free Node scripts that resolve your repo root from their own location
claims.why: Stallion's vendor promise: README says `no dependencies`, WIRING says `dependency-free Node scripts`, and a vendoring repo must be able to read both as TRUE of runtime code. The count pins that package.json carries no runtime dependencies block at all. The one deliberate exception is complexity-gate's optional typescript compiler (2026-09-20 merge wave): dev-only, optional, declared through peerDependenciesMeta — visible in the evidence set rather than hidden, because an exception nobody can see is an exception nobody can audit. NOTE: the WIRING sentence this claim anchors does not yet name the exception; the doc update should add the clause rather than this claim drifting to meet the doc. The sentence continues with the one deliberate exception (complexity-gate's optional TypeScript peer dependency, 2026-09-20 merge wave); the evidence set carries both halves — zero runtime dependencies AND the declared optional peer.

claims.anchor: The adversarial checklist — eight escape classes
claims.why: The runner's count pin and the checklist must agree: cmdDoctor enforces checklistLaneCount(checklist) === 8 and the checklist title says eight escape classes. A seventh or ninth lane drifting in silently changes what EVERY adversarial pass sweeps — one refute prompt is generated per lane — so the sweep width would change with nothing failing anywhere else.
